confer

kuhn-FUR · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To confer is to exchange opinions or ideas; to discuss something together.

The two architects stepped away from the model to confer quietly before presenting their final pitch to the client.

Example

The surgical team paused mid-operation to confer about an unexpected complication before deciding how to proceed.

Confer describes a focused, purposeful discussion between people trying to reach a decision or understanding together.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

discuss: To discuss is simply to talk something over with others -- any topic, any setting, no decision required. To confer is narrower and more purposeful: colleagues or officials pausing to exchange views because a decision has to be made. Every time people confer they discuss, but most discussion never rises to conferring.

consult: To consult is to seek information or advice from someone who knows more -- the knowledge flows one way, from expert to asker. To confer is a two-way exchange between rough equals working toward a shared decision. You consult your doctor; two doctors confer about a difficult case.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

withhold: to hold back or refuse to give

disregard: to pay no attention to something

Where it sits · how purposeful and formal the talk is — chat → confer → negotiate

chat vs. confer: A chat is casual, easygoing conversation, without the focused, purposeful exchange that confer implies.

negotiate vs. confer: Negotiate goes further than confer, aiming specifically to reach a formal agreement rather than simply exchanging views.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — con-

prefix — con-: with, together (Latin)

root — fer-

root — fer-: to carry, to bring (Latin ferre)

Put it together

Put it together: Confer comes from Latin con- ('together') plus ferre ('to carry') -- literally 'to bring together,' as ideas are brought together in discussion. The same root gives the everyday word transfer.

Use the root in a new word: transfer

Use the root in a new word: transfer: The bank transferred the funds to the new account within an hour.
